newsitem.title: USA: NYS budget plan includes $2.4 bln school bond act.
newsitem.headline: NYS budget plan includes $2.4 bln school bond act.

text.p: The New York State Assembly on Tuesday said a new pact agreed for the state's fiscal 1998 budget includes a $2.4 billion school bond act, which would have to be approved by voters in November.

"The passage of the $2.4 billion school bond issue proposal means an unprecedented opportunity for all New Yorkers to participate in a historic process that will result in funding for critical repairs to crumbling schools statewide," said Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, in prepared remarks.

The Assembly Speaker, who initially proposed a smaller, $2.0 billion school bond act, also took credit for softening some of the tough welfare changes that had been proposed by Republican Governor George Pataki.

Silver said "I am pleased that the reforms contained in this tentative agreement will be reached without the inhumane cuts to women and children." Few details about how the state would alter its welfare system were immediately available.
New York State's lawmakers missed the state's April 1 budget deadline by nearly four months, outdoing last year's dismal record when they failed to agree a new budget until July 13.

Among his victories, Silver also pointed to the planned restoration of cuts Pataki had proposed in higher education, particularly for the Tuition Assistance Program, and noted the state planned to completely end its share of clothing sales taxes on items that cost less than $100.

"Two years ago, I introduced legislation eliminating sales tax on clothing. Our sales tax experiment this year clearly demonstrated the importance of removing this tax as a means of keeping shoppers from crossing state borders to save money," Silver said. He predicted a potential economic boom from reviving the clothing industry.
Silver added that Assembly had fought hard for and won a more equitable system of providing property tax relief for middle-class families throughout the state.
